item.title: 2027: City Boy Movement targets 500,000 Enugu students for Tinubu
item.description: By Chinedu Adonu The City Boy Movement has launched a membership registration drive across tertiary institutions in Enugu State, targeting 500,000 students as part of its mobilisation efforts for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in 2027. The South-East Zonal Coordinator of the movement’s Membership Registration and Data Management, Dr. Onyeka Nwafor, disclosed this during a membership registration exercise in Enugu. Nwafor said the movement had partnered with the Council of Students’ Union Government Presidents in Enugu State (COSPEN) to expand its membership base and mobilise students across campuses in support of Tinubu’s second-term ambition. He said the initiative was aimed at strengthening the movement’s presence in the South-East and demonstrating student support for the President’s administration. Also speaking, the COSPEN Chairman and President of the Students’ Union Government of the Institute of Management and Technology (IMT), Enugu, Comrade Emmanuel Nwankwo, said student leaders had endorsed Tinubu’s re-election bid, citing the impact of the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND). Nwankwo pledged that the council would mobilise more than 500,000 students for the registration exercise. He spoke during a meeting with Nwafor at Tiger Bar, Enugu, where both parties discussed strategies for expanding membership registration and improving coordination across campuses. “Many of our peers would have dropped out of school because of financial constraints, but NELFUND has eased the burden on parents and helped students remain in school. For this, we believe Mr President deserves a second term,” he said. Describing COSPEN as the gatekeepers of tertiary institutions in the state, Nwankwo said the student loan scheme had helped address some of the financial difficulties confronting students. Nwafor, a former governorship aspirant of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Anambra State, said the movement was determined to expand its presence across tertiary institutions in the South-East. “We have resolved to scale up registration across campuses in Enugu. The registration exercise will demonstrate the level of student support for President Tinubu’s administration, particularly the impact of the student loan initiative,” he said. He added that COSPEN would coordinate the mobilisation exercise through student union presidents across the various institutions. item.title: Chinese woman accused of spying on Nvidia chief entered Taiwan 8 times
item.description: The woman accused of spying for Beijing during an affair with Nvidia founder Jensen Huang visited Taiwan a total of eight times in 2024 and 2025, a Taiwanese government minister said Thursday. Taiwan, a dominant player in the global semiconductor industry, sits at the centre of strategic competition between the United States and China, which claims the self-ruled island as part of its territory. Jensen Huang, chief executive of the US-based chip giant Nvidia, has admitted to having an extramarital affair, reportedly with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed who US officials believe was working for Chinese intelligence. Beijing has rejected the spying allegations. Alice Huang, who is also known as Huang Le, used a Hong Kong passport to enter Taiwan “under a standard business visitor status” and there were “no special flags” about her at the time, Mainland Affairs Council (MAC) Minister Chiu Chui-cheng told lawmakers. Chiu made the remarks in Taiwan’s parliament in response to lawmakers’ questions about Alice Huang’s entries into Taiwan and a New York Times report that the United States had advised Taiwan as early as 2024 to monitor her movements. “At least we at the Mainland Affairs Council did not receive any relevant information,” Chiu said. “If we had, we definitely would have stepped up our entry screening and border flow management.” Chiu said records show that Alice Huang visited Taiwan three times in 2024 and five times in 2025. The records do not show any entries for this year, he said. “If we had any of the kind of critical intelligence you mentioned, leading us to believe she posed a threat to Taiwanese society, we would have definitely flagged her for heightened review,” Chiu said. “For any case where there are doubts, we intensify the level of scrutiny, and if we determine there are security concerns, there is no way we would allow her to enter the country.” The government has said Taiwan’s security agencies are investigating the incident. Cabinet spokeswoman Michelle Lee said Thursday “there is currently no public information” about whether Alice Huang “is suspected of any criminal offence or on the related investigative procedures”. “If a criminal offence is involved, due to the principle of prosecutorial confidentiality during an ongoing investigation, we cannot provide any further comment,” Lee said. Alice Huang was seen at a dinner in May 2025 hosted by Jensen Huang at a Chinese restaurant in Taipei during Computex, the island’s top tech expo. Journalists stood outside the restaurant filming through glass windows and doors as Jensen Huang and a woman identified as Alice Huang, who was wearing a pink dress, mingled with other attendees. At one point, Jensen Huang can be seen putting his arm around Alice Huang as she kisses him on the right cheek, press livestreams show. item.title: 2027: I was told to spend N500m before contesting — Accord Party candidate, Olajengbesi
item.description: By John Alechenu ABUJA — The Accord Party candidate for Oriade/Obokun Federal Constituency, Pelumi Olajengbesi, has alleged that he was told to be prepared to throw away N500 million before he could be taken seriously as a political contender in Ijesa North. Olajengbesi made the allegation in an open letter addressed to elders and stakeholders of Ijesa North, both at home and abroad, in which he urged the people to resist what he described as an attempt to extend the tenure of the incumbent lawmaker, Wole Oke, to 28 years. A copy of the letter was made available to Vanguard in Abuja on Thursday. Recounting his first attempt to join the political race, Olajengbesi said he expressed interest in contesting for the House of Representatives in August 2016, when he was 30 years old and had limited financial resources. He alleged that Hon. Niyi Ajifowobaje, whom he described as one of Oke’s prominent political associates at the time, told him that an aspirant in Ijesa North must be prepared to throw N500 million into a river before considering a contest for the Oriade/Obokun seat. According to him, Ajifowobaje further suggested that an aspirant would need as much as N1 billion to be taken seriously. “I was told to throw away N500 million before running in Ijesa North,” he said. Olajengbesi said he subsequently assembled a group of young people in the constituency on July 11, 2017, to examine the incumbent’s political strengths and identify alternative approaches to representation. He said the group produced a 16-page report, which he had incorporated into a book he was writing. According to him, the report concluded that money was the major political advantage the incumbent brought to the table, rather than ideas, innovation or inspiration for younger generations. “Money was the only thing he was bringing to the table. No ideas, no innovation, no inspiration, no storytelling, nothing to inspire younger people. Just money without excellence,” he quoted the report as saying. He said the report also observed that several professionals and educated people in the constituency were dissatisfied with the quality of representation but were reluctant to support a challenger unless they were convinced the person had sufficient financial resources to sustain the contest. Olajengbesi alleged that the incumbent had cultivated an image of political dominance that made some potential challengers believe they could not compete with his financial strength. He further alleged that Oke once boasted during a private conversation about his election spending and how he had dealt with previous challengers. According to Olajengbesi, Oke allegedly claimed to have paid for the return journeys of some aspirants based abroad and financially settled local contenders. He declined to identify the individuals allegedly mentioned in the conversation. item.title: 2027: INEC must earn voters’ trust before election day — IPC
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The International Press Centre (IPC) has urged officials of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to build public confidence in the electoral body ahead of the 2027 general elections through transparent conduct, accurate information and effective communication. The Executive Director of IPC, Dr. Lanre Arogundade, said public trust in the commission must be established long before election day, warning that misinformation, disinformation and inaccurate communication could undermine the credibility of the electoral process. Arogundade spoke on Wednesday in Kano at a two-day capacity-building engagement for INEC’s Voter Education and Publicity (VEP) and gender officials on electoral trust, effective communication, legal literacy and voter engagement. He noted that INEC had become a major subject of public discussions surrounding the elections, including disagreements among political parties and their supporters, even when the commission was not directly involved in such disputes. He said the manner in which INEC officials respond to public concerns and clarify issues could either strengthen or weaken confidence in the electoral body. “Every public interaction can either deposit or withdraw institutional trust,” he said. Arogundade explained that the training was designed to deepen the officials’ understanding of the Electoral Act, improve their communication skills, prepare them for crisis situations and equip them with the ability to verify and respond to false information. He stressed that VEP officials must be able to explain electoral laws and procedures in simple language, particularly when disputes arise or tensions develop during the electoral process. He warned that inaccurate responses to questions about electoral laws and voting procedures could damage the commission’s credibility more than withholding an answer. “A vague or inaccurate answer from a VEP official, for example, on legal questions around the Electoral Act or voting procedures can cost the commission more than silence would,” he said. The IPC director also called on INEC to establish dedicated fact-checking units in its state offices to identify and respond promptly to false information circulating about the commission. He said the officials would be introduced to social media listening techniques to monitor conversations about INEC in their respective states and provide clarifications where necessary. Arogundade expressed concern over the growing use of artificial intelligence to generate misleading content, noting that voices could be cloned within minutes and election result sheets falsified within seconds. Also speaking, the Executive Director of the Centre for Media and Society (CEMESO), Dr. Akin Akingbulu, said building public trust required more than issuing public statements, urging INEC to match its promises with concrete actions. “Walk the talk. item.title: Two French Guards Collapse As Macron Welcomes Slovak President
item.description: Two members of France’s elite Republican Guard collapsed almost simultaneously outside the Elysee Palace as President Emmanuel Macron welcomed his Slovak counterpart, according to televised images and a presidential source. As is customary for the arrival of foreign heads of state, the Republican Guards formed an honour guard in full ceremonial dress with sabres for the arrival of Slovak President Peter Pellegrini late Wednesday. One guard can be seen swaying before crashing to the ground, falling against a pillar at the Elysee Palace as his ceremonial sword clattered to the ground. France’s President Emmanuel Macron (R) bids farewell to Slovakia’s President Peter Pellegrini following their meeting at the Elysee presidential Palace in Paris on November 11, 2026. (Photo by Guillaume Saligot / AFP) | Guillaume Saligot / AFP Aides and Macron immediately rushed towards the stricken guard, images from an AFP photographer showed. Le Parisien daily said that a second guard collapsed off camera, with Macron looking concerned and then hurriedly welcoming his Slovak counterpart. A French presidential source, who asked not to be named, told AFP that both guards had suffered from “fainting attacks” and no other comment would be made. “Both of them were swiftly taken care of, and everything is fine,” added the source. The Republican Guard, part of the French gendarmerie, is responsible for guards of honour in France, which often involve standing for long periods in heavy clothing while holding their sword vertically. France’s President Emmanuel Macron (L) and other officials attend to a Republican Guard who fainted while standing at attention, as he waits the arrival of Slovakia’s President at the Elysee Palace in Paris on November 11, 2026. item.title: Nvidia board meets over Jensen Huang’s future after affair revelations
item.description: CEO Jensen Huang’s future with Nvidia was unclear Thursday as the chip giant’s board was reported to have met after revelations he had two extramarital affairs, including with a woman accused of spying for China. The scandal has sent shares of the multi-trillion dollar behemoth plunging and left uncertain the fate of Huang, who has been a key promoter of the artificial intelligence boom. Huang, 63, has spent years lobbying against curbs on sales of advanced AI chips to China, and US President Donald Trump last year cleared Nvidia’s H200 chips for export there over objections from Beijing’s critics in both parties. The chip giant’s board met on Wednesday to weigh Huang’s future, according to CNN and the New York Times. Nvidia has not made any statements about the outcome of the meeting. Beijing has rejected the spying allegations. Nvidia shares were down around 25 percent from their all-time high in early October and the scandal has raised questions over who could replace Huang if he is ousted. The rapidly unfolding story exploded after reports that Huang, who has been married to Lori Huang for over 40 years, was involved in an extramarital romance. The Nvidia CEO has since admitted to having an affair, reportedly with Alice Huang, who was a senior executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed. US intelligence reportedly circulated a memo this past spring alleging Alice Huang was an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. Alice Huang was among the attendees at a dinner hosted by Jensen Huang at a Chinese restaurant in Taipei on May 22, 2025, during Computex, the island’s top tech expo. At one point, Jensen Huang can be seen putting his arm around Alice Huang as she kisses him on the right cheek, press livestreams show. She visited Taiwan a total of eight times in 2024 and 2025, a Taiwanese government minister said Thursday. Nvidia’s board had already announced on Sunday a probe of what it called reporting that Jensen Huang had been the target of a “foreign intelligence effort”. Then came on Wednesday New York Times reporting that the Nvidia co-founder was involved in a second extramarital affair, saying there was video evidence of the 63-year-old executive being affectionate with Nvidia’s vice president of health care, Kimberly Powell. Powell, 48, has been a public face of Nvidia’s efforts to expand the chip technology into higher education and health care, and was speaking at a San Jose, California conference where they “were seen being affectionate at the hotel” by bystanders, the Times reported. The chip giant’s code of conduct tells associates to avoid conflicts of interest, and cites the example of “personal relationships”. “We avoid situations where our actions might create a conflict — actual or potential — between our personal gain and our obligations to Nvidia”, the code says. – Possible ouster – Nvidia’s bylaws require a majority of the 11 board directors to remove Huang as CEO. item.title: Withheld ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍‌​‍‍⁠​​‌​LG funds: Osun workers resume after three-day warning strike
item.description: Government workers in Osun resumed duty on Thursday after putting off their three-day warning strike called by the organiser labour for the release of funds due to local governments in the state by the Federal Government. The News of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the gates of the state government secretariat in Abere and Osun Assembly, shut since Monday, were reopened with workers back to work. Similarly, workers in Olorunda and Osogbo Local Government Secretariats were also back to their duty posts. NAN reports that organised labour in the state had on Sunday directed workers to embarked on solidarity strike with local government workers for the release of the withheld council allocations. The organised labour comprising the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), Trade Union Congress (TUC) and Joint Negotiating Council (JNC), however, on Wednesday directed workers to resume duty today. The organised labour appreciated workers, pensioners and affiliate unions for their support, cooperation and peaceful conduct during the industrial action. “The organised labour expresses its profound appreciation to all affiliate unions, workers, pensioners and members for their unwavering solidarity, cooperation and exemplary conduct throughout the three-day sympathy strike in support of the Nigeria Union of Local Government Employees (NULGE), Osun Council. “We commend all members for their commitment, discipline, unity and peaceful conduct during the industrial action. “Your solidarity has once again demonstrated the strength of the labour movement and our collective resolve to defend workers’ rights, welfare and dignity. “Accordingly, all workers are hereby directed to resume work at midnight Nov. 11. “All affiliate unions and their members are enjoined to comply fully with this directive and return to their respective workplaces,” it said. The organised labour urged workers to remain calm, united and steadfast, while maintaining mobilisation and remaining on standby for further directives. item.title: Sales Hack Conference 2026: Nnamani leads six industry experts to Abuja
item.description: By Chioma Okoye The Convener of the Sales Hack Conference, Chinedu Paul Nnamani, is set to bring together six professionals from the business, technology, entrepreneurship, media and management sectors for the 2026 edition of the conference scheduled to hold in Abuja on Saturday, November 14. The conference, themed “Explosive Sales: Market Smart, Convert More, Earn Big,” is aimed at equipping entrepreneurs, business owners, marketers and sales professionals with practical strategies for improving sales performance, attracting customers and growing sustainable businesses. The event is expected to attract business owners, corporate professionals, students and other stakeholders for discussions on sales strategies, market positioning, customer psychology and business growth. According to the organisers, the conference is designed to provide a platform for sharing practical business knowledge, professional experience and industry insights to help individuals and organisations strengthen their sales capabilities. The 2026 edition will feature speakers drawn from different areas of the business and professional ecosystem. They include Dr. Jamie Pajoel, Founder and Global President of Jamie Pajoel International; Kel Armstrong Amobi, Founder and Host of KaaTruths Podcast; Dr. Ninnah Samuel, a business and technology law expert; Ajah Excel, Chief Executive Officer of Silicon Africa and Convener of SMfest; and Abraham Ofure Orukpe, a business management consultant and coach. Nnamani will also feature as convener, coordinating the engagement between the speakers and participants. The organisers said the diversity of the speakers was intended to provide participants with perspectives on different aspects of sales development, including business strategy, technology, communication, consumer behaviour, legal considerations and management. Discussions will focus on practical sales techniques, buying behaviour, customer acquisition and retention, relationship building, revenue generation and strategies for competing in an increasingly demanding marketplace. The conference is also expected to provide networking opportunities for entrepreneurs, corporate professionals and emerging talents to establish business relationships and explore potential collaborations. The organisers said the event would be particularly relevant to Nigerian businesses navigating changing consumer expectations, increasing market competition and the need to develop sustainable revenue streams. The conference will hold at Centre Point Event Centre, Centre Shehu Shagari Way, Wuse, Abuja, beginning at 8 a.m. West Africa Time. Registration is available under four categories: Basic, N5,000; Executive, N15,000; Premium, N30,000; and VIP, N70,000. Further information and registration are available through the conference’s official website. item.title: Updated: Manchester United sack coach Carrick
item.description: Manchester United sacked manager Michael Carrick on Thursday after their worst-ever start to a Premier League campaign, with USA boss Mauricio Pochettino expected to replace him. Former United midfielder Carrick led the team to an impressive third-place finish last season but they have taken just eight points from 10 games in the current campaign and are mired in the relegation zone. “Manchester United can confirm that Michael Carrick has departed his role as men’s first-team head coach,” the club said in a statement. It added: “After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions.” Carrick’s final game in charge was a chaotic 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday, after which he stressed he would not walk away and was looking to the international break as usual. But the United hierarchy have decided to act in the hope of saving their season after a paltry three wins in all competitions. Former Tottenham, Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain boss Pochettino would have an enormous task on his hands to revive a club that has never recovered from the departure of Alex Ferguson 13 years ago. The Red Devils, once the dominant force in English football, have been overtaken by Manchester City, Liverpool and Arsenal. United’s next game is against fierce rivals Liverpool at Anfield on November 22. The post Updated: Manchester United sack coach Carrick appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Angola celebrates 51st independence anniversary, acknowledges Nigeria’s support
item.description: The Angola Embassy in Nigeria has commended Nigeria’s support for the country’s independence, attained in 1975. Dr José Zau, Angola’s Head of Mission to Nigeria, Benin, Niger and ECOWAS, said this at the celebration of the 51st anniversary of independence on Wednesday night in Abuja. Zau described relations between the two countries as a strategic, historic and fraternal partnership, anchored in political alignment as leading African oil producers. He said Nigeria played a significant role in supporting Angola’s independence process and the consolidation of the Angolan state. “Through the Bilateral Joint Commission, the two nations have been updating and expanding dozens of agreements and memoranda of understanding. “These cover trade, transport, culture, professional training, defence and public order, cybersecurity, and academic exchange,” he said. He cited a visa-exemption agreement for holders of diplomatic and official passports, and twinning partnerships between Angolan provinces and Nigerian states, as measures to deepen ties. The twinning pairs the Namibe and Bengo provinces with the Bayelsa and Nasarawa states, he said. He said relations were strengthened by engagement between Angolan President João Lourenço and Nigerian President Bola Tinubu. Zau said the Caculo Cabaça Dam would become operational in June 2027, with the capacity to generate at least 2,172 megawatts (MW). He said the dam would raise Angola’s total capacity from 6,400 MW to about 8,600 MW. He also highlighted the country’s achievements in 2026. item.title: Erdogan Urges Return To Diplomacy To End Iran-US Conflict
item.description: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan on Thursday said diplomacy should resume “without further delay” to end the US-Iran war after talks with his Iranian counterpart. Erdogan met Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian on the sidelines of the UN climate conference in the Turkish province of Antalya, his office said. During their discussion, Erdogan underscored “the importance of getting to the negotiating table without further delay” and said Turkey would continue to support efforts aimed at securing peace. “Common ground for agreement must be strengthened and diplomacy given a chance,” he said, expressing hope that the conflict with the US “would end as soon as possible”. The Middle East war broke out on February 28 with US-Israeli strikes that killed Iran’s supreme leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. Iran responded by launching missiles and drones at countries across the region, while the militant groups it backs in Lebanon, Yemen and Iraq also entered the fray. Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian leaves after delivering a speech during the High-Level Segment for Heads of States and Government at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) at the Antalya Expo Center in Antalya on November 11, 2026. Photo by OZAN KOSE / AFP In an address to the UN climate summit on Wednesday, Pezeshkian accused the United States and Israel of inflicting severe environmental damage during attacks on the Islamic Republic. “The recent criminal and illegal aggression against Iran by America and the Zionist regime… has inflicted severe damage on the environment, releasing massive quantities of pollutants and greenhouse gases into the atmosphere,” he said. Diplomatic efforts led by Qatar and Pakistan have sought to negotiate an end to the war. Tehran wants Washington to accept a raft of demands including unfreezing assets and lifting sanctions in return for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, the vital energy conduit it has blockaded since the start of the conflict. The ruling followed a suit filed by Nafiu Bala Gombe, a former National Deputy Chairman of the party, who challenged the process through which Mark and other members of the committee assumed leadership after the resignation of former National Chairman, Ralph Nwosu. The court’s decision was reported to have affected the process that produced Atiku as the party’s presidential candidate, as the Mark-led committee organised the primary election. The ADC, however, rejected the judgment, describing it as legally indefensible and accusing the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of seeking to weaken the opposition. The party also said it would challenge the decision, citing an earlier judgment by Justice Musa Liman of the same Federal High Court, which it said had affirmed the legitimacy of the Mark-led leadership. Speaking further on ADC’s standpoint on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief on Thursday, Kola Ologbondiyan, Spokesperson of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, accused the APC of working toward coronating Tinubu in 2027 instead of allowing for healthy competition. Ologbondiyan alleged that the APC has given no room for opposition politics. “So it now goes into what we have been saying because what we now want is that no candidate must stand against during the election, and that goes to nothing as far as we are concerned in the African Democratic Congress.” The ADC’s Spokesperson said that his party has taken the necessary steps to appeal the judgement. “We are sure that we will go to the next level in the administration of justice; we believe that all this manipulation and attempt to suppress Nigerians, all this move to dismantle democratic structures will not work. item.title: Floyd Mayweather To Launch TMT Frontrow Fight Series In Nigeria
item.description: ABUJA, NIGERIA – 11 November 2026 – Boxing legend Floyd “Money” Mayweather will arrive in Abuja on Thursday, 12 November, to announce the launch of the TMT Frontrow Fight Series Nigeria and explore investment opportunities in Nigeria’s mining and solid minerals sector. The initiative aims to identify, train and promote young Nigerian boxing talent through the Frontrow Fight Series boxing academies and grassroots development programmes across Lagos, Abuja, Enugu, Calabar and other locations. The first TMT Frontrow Fight Series event is planned for 2027, with Floyd Mayweather also fighting in Nigeria during the same year. ABUJA PRESS CONFERENCE Mayweather will address the media in Abuja on Friday, 13 November 2026, to outline the Frontrow Fight Series and its plans to develop and empower Nigerian youth through boxing. BANGKOK FIGHT – 19 DECEMBER 2026 Mayweather will also discuss his upcoming fight in Bangkok, Thailand, against Australian light heavyweight boxer Matt “The Jedi” Floyd, who has a professional record of 15 wins from 17 fights. Further details of the fight, including how Nigerian boxing fans can subscribe to watch the event, will be announced at the Abuja press conference. Some go for the beaches, some for the shopping, and others just want to see the famous Burj Khalifa up close. But before you book your flight, there is one important thing to take care of first, your visa. The good news is that getting a UAE tourist visa is easier than it used to be. Most of the process happens online, and your visa comes straight to your email. Still, the rules are not the same for every traveller. Some people get a visa on arrival, while others must apply before they fly. A few small mistakes can also slow things down or even get your application rejected. So let us walk through what you really need to know before you pack your bags. Do Nigerian Travellers Need a Visa for the UAE? Yes, Nigerian travellers need a visa to enter the United Arab Emirates for tourism. The UAE lets travellers from some countries enter without a visa, or get one when they land. But Nigeria is not on that list. If you hold a Nigerian passport, you must apply for your UAE tourist visa before you fly. That means you cannot just show up at Dubai International Airport and sort things out there. Your visa must be approved and in your inbox before you check in for your flight. The process is not hard, though. With the right documents and a trusted service, most people get through it without any stress. Whether this is your first trip or your fifth, this guide will help you from start to finish. UAE Tourist Visa Types: Picking the Right One for Your Trip The UAE offers a few tourist visa options. Some let you enter only once. Others let you come and go many times. The validity period also changes from one visa to another. For example, a visa might be valid for 60 days, but it may only let you stay for 30 days inside the country. Always read the details before you book your flight. item.title: Indonesian Vice President Resigns In High School Diploma Scandal
item.description: Indonesia’s vice president resigned Thursday, undone by a scandal over his high school diploma that has added to pressure on a government facing widespread dissatisfaction over the economy, graft and wildfires. There had been repeated calls for Gibran Rakabuming Raka, 39, to step down following a Supreme Court ruling last month to annul his high school qualification, obtained abroad. On Thursday, he submitted his resignation to President Prabowo Subianto and to parliament. Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka (C) arrives at the vice president’s palace after submitting his resignation letter to the People’s Consultative Assembly in Jakarta on November 12, 2026. Photo by ABIMANYU / AFP Prabowo told reporters he had accepted Gibran’s resignation “with a heavy heart” and praised him for acting “for a greater cause, for the interests of the nation, the state, and the people of Indonesia”. “He certainly feels that he has pursued his education through an orderly process, but we all understand that the education system abroad is different from the education system in Indonesia,” the president said. Indonesia’s vice president does not have many constitutionally defined powers apart from acting as the president’s representative at official events and taking over if his boss is incapacitated. ‘Political realignment’ Gibran’s downfall came after thousands of Indonesians took to the streets in recent weeks to protest economic hardship, graft, perceived authoritarianism and the government’s handling of months of devastating wildfires emitting toxic haze. University students protest demanding a government review including lowering the prices of basic commodities, military involvement in civilian affairs, free meal program, taxation of sanitary pads and addressing the issue of wildfires in Surabaya on November 10, 2026. (Photo by Juni KRISWANTO / AFP) | Juni KRISWANTO / AFP His exit is likely to complicate a loose governing alliance that includes the parties of Prabowo and of his predecessor Joko Widodo — Gibran’s father, who goes by Jokowi. The resignation “marks a significant political realignment, but does not necessarily threaten government stability”, according to Khairul Fahmi, executive director of the Institute for Security and Strategic Studies (ISESS) think tank. “Jokowi will retain political influence, but Gibran’s departure could reduce his network’s direct access to power. For Prabowo, this creates greater room to consolidate his leadership and pursue his own political agenda,” Khairul told AFP. Two years into his term, Prabowo’s popularity has reached record lows. Last week, Indonesian authorities arrested the former national police chief and three senior police officials for allegedly tapping the president’s telephone. On Thursday, police said they were investigating possible treason. Prabowo’s rise to power was widely credited to support from the popular Jokowi, who served two terms from 2014 to 2024. item.title: Nvidia preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang: US media
item.description: Nvidia’s board is preparing to oust its co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang, US media reported Wednesday, as the chip giant’s chief faces new accusations of infidelity, after revelations he had an affair with a woman accused of spying for China. The tech company’s board was preparing to meet as soon as Wednesday to determine Huang’s future, according to the Wall Street Journal, which quoted people familiar with the matter. The New York Times reported Wednesday that Huang was also involved in a second extramarital affair, with a subordinate, saying there was video evidence of the 63-year-old executive being affectionate with Nvidia’s vice president of health care, Kimberly Powell. Powell, 48, has been a public face of Nvidia’s efforts to expand the chip technology into higher education and health care, and was speaking at a San Jose, California conference where they “were seen being affectionate at the hotel” by bystanders, the Times reported. The report of the second affair follows Huang’s acknowledgment of a relationship with Alice Huang, a senior executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed. The Wall Street Journal reported that the two were photographed together in Taipei in 2024 and 2025. US intelligence reportedly circulated a memo this past spring alleging Alice Huang was an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. The Nvidia CEO admitted to having had a relationship with Huang — to whom he bears no familial relation — in a note to Nvidia employees Sunday, writing: “I was unfaithful to my wife.” The same day Nvidia’s board of directors said in a statement that they’d launched “an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.” “I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company,” Huang wrote in his statement. He has also been called on by Congress to provide a closed-door briefing on his interactions with Alice Huang, the Times reported. As the artificial intelligence industry surge has spurred Nvidia’s stock prices to new heights, Huang has appeared at US President Donald Trump’s side at White House events, as recently as last month when he accepted a National Medal of Science from the Republican leader. Huang was among the world’s most influential tech leaders — including Elon Musk, Jeff Bezos and Mark Zuckerberg — who vowed to self-regulate AI against possible threats, as Trump rejected calls for government oversight and dismissed warnings the technology could wipe out humanity. Nvidia shareholders filed a class action lawsuit against Huang and the AI chip maker for failing to disclose information about the relationship to investors. Nvidia shares have plummeted in recent days since Huang admitted to the affair. item.title: COP31: UK Makes History, Appoints World’s First ‘Climate Security’ Envoy
item.description: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced on Thursday the appointment of a special envoy focused on “climate security”, a world first, to better prepare for the growing impacts of global warming. In a speech to the UN’s COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, the Labour leader recalled that he spent his first three weeks as prime minister this past summer responding to the worst wildfires Britain ever experienced. “I decided then it was important for me to be here to show British leadership in a world where climate issues have taken too much of a backseat,” said Burnham, who was the only G7 leader attending the summit. UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres delivers a speech during the High-Level Segment for Heads of States and Government at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) at the Antalya Expo Center in Antalya on November 11, 2026. Britain and the rest of western Europe experienced their hottest summer on record, with a succession of heatwaves and wildfires. The heat caused tens of thousands of excess deaths on the continent. “Climate is a national security issue,” Burnham said. “As evidence of that, I am today announcing the appointment of Dame Madeleine Alessandri as the first UK special representative for climate security,” he said. Swedish activist Greta Thunberg arrives at the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, on November 10, 2026. Alessandri is the former head of the UK’s Joint Intelligence Committee, the body that briefs ministers on security threats. “In this role, I will work with partners across government and internationally to strengthen our understanding of climate threats, build resilience, and ensure we are better prepared for the challenges ahead,” Alessandri said in a statement. Brazil’s President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva delivers a speech during the High-Level Segment for Heads of States and Government at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) at the Antalya Expo Center in Antalya on November 11, 2026. Photo by OZAN KOSE / AFP Britain has a climate minister, Katie White, who is in Antalya for the COP31 talks that are scheduled to end on November 20. Cosima Cassel, an expert at climate think-tank E3G, said countries often have climate envoys and climate security is part of their remit. “This is the first climate security envoy specifically,” she told AFP. “This appointment elevates that issue to the level it deserves, and other governments should consider a similar model,” Cassel said. Environmental group Greenpeace also said the appointment was a “welcome move” as climate change is a “threat multiplier”. item.title: Court orders extradition of Nigerian to US over alleged wire fraud, others
item.description: The Federal High Court in Abuja has ordered the extradition of a Nigerian, Temitope Omotade, to the U.S. District Court of Minnesota to face his trial over allegations bordering on wire fraud, among others. Justice Peter Lifu, in a judgment, held that the application made by the Attorney-General of the Federation (AGF) was meritorious. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the AGF had made the application for the extradition of Omotade to the U.S. He is a suspect in a superseding five-count indictment bordering on five counts in case number 22-CR-24 SRN/HB filed on Feb. 8, 2022, at the US District Court. The offences in counts one, two and three bordered on mail and wire fraud in violation of Title 18 US Code, Sections 1341 and 1343, and 1349, which carries a maximum penalty of 30 years in prison in each of the counts. Counts four and five bordered on aggravated identity theft and aiding and abetting, in violation of Title 18 US Codes, Sections 1028A (a)(1) and 2, which carries a maximum penalty of two years in prison for each count, consecutive to any other term of imprisonment imposed on the defendant. In the AGF’s application, he contended that the request was grounded on an extradition packet and diplomatic notes from the US, including a sealed indictment from the U.S. District Court for the District of Minnesota and a warrant for Omotade’s arrest. He argued that all statutory requirements under the Extradition Act have been met because the offences are non-political, non-trivial, and made in good faith. He submitted that the Central Authority Unit had established that proper certifications and documentation, including affidavits from US officials, relevant statute copies, and passport details, accompanied the formal request. Besides, the AGF said there were no pending local criminal proceedings in Nigeria against Omotade for the specified offences, and adequate assurances regarding nonprejudicial trial conditions in the US had been secured. He asserted that the request and accompanying materials satisfied all conditions for the surrender of Omotade, who was the sole respondent in the suit marked FHC/ABJ/CS/494/2024. The AGF maintained that the legal procedures complied with the Oaths Act and the Extradition Act, adding that the interest of justice dictated that the request be granted, “as the respondent is duly accused of the indictments brought against him abroad.” But Omotade, in his counter-affidavit filed by his lawyer, prayed the court to dismiss the suit. Omotade denied all allegations of mail fraud, wire fraud, conspiracy, and aggravated identity theft, maintaining that his connection to Roxanne Gilbert involved no criminal conduct or digital proceeds. He contended that the extradition application lacked substantive proof and statutory backing for several reasons. item.title: Oil: Nigeria cautions Namibia against host community neglect
item.description: By Folarin Kehinde Nigeria has urged Namibia to establish clear policies on host community benefits, local content development and environmental protection before commencing commercial oil production, warning the emerging oil-producing country against repeating the challenges that have characterised Nigeria’s petroleum industry. Nigeria’s High Commissioner to Namibia, Ambassador Esther Adebola Arewa, gave the advice while delivering the keynote address titled: Nigeria-Namibia at the 5th International African Energy, Oil and Gas Summit in Windhoek, Namibia. Arewa said Namibia could draw important lessons from Nigeria’s nearly seven decades of oil exploration, particularly its experiences with gas flaring, community grievances, regulatory uncertainty and inadequate local participation. She urged the Namibian government to make adequate provisions for communities in oil-producing areas before the first barrel of crude oil is produced. “Decide now, before the first barrel, how the people of ǁKaras and the coastal towns will share in this, and write it down,” she said. The envoy stressed that establishing trust with host communities before production begins would help prevent conflicts and costly disputes in the future. “It is far cheaper to build trust before production than to buy back peace afterwards,” she added. Her warning comes as Namibia advances petroleum exploration in the Orange Basin, which has attracted significant international interest. Arewa identified gas utilisation, regulatory certainty, local content development and host community participation as four major lessons Namibia should draw from Nigeria’s experience. On gas utilisation, she said Nigeria had wasted substantial quantities of associated gas through flaring for decades but had made progress in reducing the practice. She disclosed that nearly 93 per cent of the gas produced in Nigeria in the first half of 2026 was put to use, while the country’s gas reserves stood at about 215 trillion cubic feet. She said Nigeria was willing to share its technical expertise with Namibia, particularly in managing associated gas from offshore petroleum operations. On regulatory reforms, Arewa recalled that Nigeria spent more than a decade debating comprehensive petroleum legislation before the Petroleum Industry Act was enacted in August 2021. According to her, the prolonged uncertainty affected investor confidence and drove some investors away. “Investors waited. Some of them left. Certainty, even imperfect certainty, is worth a great deal,” she said. The High Commissioner also cited Nigeria’s local content policy as an example of how deliberate government intervention could increase domestic participation in the oil and gas industry. She said Nigerian content in the petroleum sector rose from about 26 per cent in 2016 to 61 per cent in 2026, with a target of 70 per cent. item.title: FG urged to engage Oyedepo, Ibiyeomie, Enenche, Komaiya on development
item.description: The Federal Government has been urged to engage prominent Nigerian Christian leaders, including Bishop David Oyedepo, Pastor David Ibiyeomie, Dr Paul Enenche and Pastor Korede Komaiya, to explore how their religious institutions could contribute to addressing the country’s development challenges. The Convener of the Christian Youth Forum, James Paul Adama, made the call in an article titled, “Why the Nigerian Government Must Invite Bishop David Oyedepo and His Spiritual Sons Immediately.” Adama argued that the institutions established by the clerics had developed structures and community-based initiatives that could provide useful lessons for national development. He said the institutions combined academic development with character building to prepare young Nigerians for leadership and responsible citizenship. On healthcare, he cited medical outreaches, financial assistance to patients, sponsorship of surgeries and support for Nigerians seeking specialised medical treatment abroad. He added that scholarship programmes operated by the churches had helped young people from disadvantaged backgrounds gain access to education and professional qualifications. The development advocate further identified investments in electricity generation, road construction, pedestrian bridges and water facilities as evidence of the institutions’ capacity to deliver infrastructure within their areas of operation. On employment, Adama claimed that the four church organisations collectively provided jobs for more than 300,000 people. He said their operations extended beyond religious activities to education, healthcare, administration, hospitality, logistics and other sectors of the economy. Beyond infrastructure and economic activities, Adama highlighted the role of the religious institutions in counselling, moral instruction, family development and entrepreneurship training. He argued that their programmes could offer useful insights into addressing social challenges, strengthening families and promoting responsible citizenship. item.title: Trump to flex muscles on Asia tour after midterms losses
item.description: After his party suffered a midterms hammering, President Donald Trump faces a new challenge: proving he is still the boss of US foreign policy on the global stage. With Trump politically hamstrung as he enters the remaining two-year ‘lame duck’ period of his White House tenure, world leaders may be quietly wondering how to leverage the new balance of power in Washington. The 80-year-old Republican heads to the ASEAN summit in the Philippines and APEC summit in China from a radically transformed and hostile political landscape at home after the Democrats seized both the House of Representatives and Senate. Constitutionally banned from seeking a third term in the 2028 presidential race, the unpredictable billionaire could be all the more inclined to focus his energy on the international stage. “After bad midterms, this is how presidents reset,” Edgard Kagan, an expert at the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) told a news briefing. – Iran, trade, China – That is especially true for Trump on his Asian tour, where he is unlikely to be pressed publicly on domestic politics. China has described the midterms as an “internal affair” and said it is “willing to continue working” with the United States after Republicans lost control of both chambers of Congress. But the power shift in Washington will still be on leaders’ radars, said Joshua Kurlantzick, an expert in Southeast Asia and South Asia at the Council on Foreign Relations. “In private, many (Asian) leaders are relieved,” Kurlantzick wrote in an article this month. “The Iran war has been particularly challenging for the United States’ Asian partners and allies, and they hope that after the midterm results US President Donald Trump’s decision-making on the issue will become more predictable.” Trump has said several times since the midterms that renewed fighting between the United States and Iran is unlikely. A Democratic-controlled Congress could also take a tougher stance towards China, Kurlantzick added, backtracking on the Trump administration’s “soft approach” to Beijing that has sparked unease among US allies in Asia. Leaders in the world’s largest continent are also hoping to see Democrats push back on Trump’s barrage of tariffs on trading partners, which have stung Asian economies heavily reliant on exports. Democratic House leader Hakeem Jeffries has urged Congress to reassert its authority over US trade policy. The Democrats will not get an easy ride in undoing Trump’s policies, though. The president enjoys broad authority over trade and holds veto power over congressional legislation — which he has vowed to use. – High-profile meeting – Trump relishes dramatic gestures and foreign policy provides an ideal arena for high-profile meetings, such as with Chinese and Russian leaders Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin. item.title: Who could potentially replace Jensen Huang if Nvidia ousts him?
item.description: Chip giant Nvidia’s board was reportedly meeting Wednesday to discuss the future of co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang after he dated an accused Chinese spy, according to US media. The 63-year-old tech titan, who has led the key AI giant since it was founded in 1993, has been beleaguered with reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including with Alice Huang, a data center executive who has been accused by US intelligence of working for China’s Ministry of State Security. With Huang unexpectedly on the backfoot, and no known plan of succession at Nvidia, the field is wide open for a variety of replacements to lead one of the key AI players should the board decide to oust Huang. Here are some of the names being suggested most frequently as Huang’s potential successor. Internal hire With over 40,000 employees, Nvidia could opt to go with an in-house pick to take the helm, including one of Huang’s dozens of direct reports. Tech publications frequently cited Nvidia’s Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as an easy choice, if for no other reason than she is already among top leadership at the chip behemoth. Another longtime Nvidia honcho is Ian Buck, who oversees the company’s data center clients. He was a key mind behind the software that keeps Nvidia-designed chips in demand. Business magazine Inc. also lists Nvidia’s vice president of applied deep learning research, Bryan Catanzaro, as a possible pick. A family affair Huang could also try and position a member of his own family as his replacement, with more than one option for a bloodline succession. His daughter Madison Huang is currently the senior director of product marketing at Nvidia and is among the names most suggested by analysts. As a marketing leader, she had a multi-year stint at luxury conglomerate LVMH. Jensen Huang’s son Spencer Huang could also be a potential successor. He currently works at Nvidia as the director of product management in the company’s robotics division. Huang’s cousin, Lisa Su, could also be a viable candidate for selection – not only is she his first cousin, once removed, but she also has valuable expertise as the longtime CEO of semiconductor giant AMD. Tech CEO swap Su is not the only tech chief being bandied around as a possible replacement for Huang. Rene Haas, CEO of UK chip design firm Arm, is another candidate being suggested by the tech press. Speculation runs wide in Silicon Valley, where former Apple CEO Tim Cook – who stepped down from leading the tech giant in August after 15 years at the helm – is another person insiders say could potentially be tapped. item.title: Student Loan: Parents, NANS offer tips on how to stop double dipping by beneficiaries
item.description: By Adesina Wahab Parents under the aegis of National Parent Teacher Association of Nigeria, NAPTAN, and the National Association of Nigerian Students, NANS, have offered tips on how to stop the practice of students benefitting from the Student Loan Scheme and still going ahead to collect tuition fees from their parents and guardians. The practice, labelled double dipping by the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, NELFUND, which gives out the loans, is gradually becoming rampant and erasing the main reason the loan scheme was initiated – take the burden of tuition payment off the necks of parents and guardians. Speaking with Thursday Learning, the Chairman of the Board of Trustees of NAPTAN, Chief Deolu Ogunbanjo, opined that such a practice negates the reason for the setting up of the scheme. “The Student Loan Scheme was set up to give access to higher education to students who would otherwise drop out because of inability to pay fees. It is also to take the burden of fee payment off the necks of parents and guardians. Such happenings may not be totally eradicated. We know how rascally some young ones can be. “I think the way out is to let the parents and guardians be aware when payments are made by NELFUND to beneficiaries. Let there be a means of notifying the parents that their children have benefitted from the scheme,” he said Similarly, the National Public Relations Officer of NANS, Comrade Obidah David, also supported notification being sent to parents of beneficiaries. “If it is a text message, they can send to parents and guardians of beneficiaries. Information on contacts of parents is always provided by students when registering. That is necessary in case of any emergency. Also, names of beneficiaries can be published whether in the traditional media or social media. There is nothing bad in that. It is for transparency, “ he stated. Recall that recently, the Managing Director of NELFUND, Akintunde Sawyerr, said during a press briefing that the fund had identified cases of students allegedly accessing loan support while continuing to place the burden of tuition payments on their parents. Describing the practice as unacceptable, Sawyerr said the fund was determined to end the situation and strengthen transparency in the administration of the scheme. “This comment is based on our recognition that there are so many students out there who are double-dipping. They are taking from NELFUND and still stressing their parents. We are going to put an end to that,” he said. Under the proposed arrangement, parents would be able to confirm whether their children’s school fees had been paid through NELFUND without necessarily having access to the actual amount involved. Sawyerr said the initiative was intended to address concerns among parents who continued to shoulder the financial responsibilities of their children’s education despite the availability of government-backed loans. item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 12, 2026
item.description: The Nigerian naira opened trading on Thursday, November 12, 2026, under sustained demand pressure across both the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) and the parallel market, maintaining the wider spread observed earlier in the week. At the official window, data from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) shows the naira entering Thursday’s session around the ₦1,350.36 to ₦1,353.50 per dollar band. Early Thursday morning international currency feeds recorded spot quotes hovering near ₦1,345.72 per dollar, while official NFEM benchmarks reflect the closing figures from the prior trading session pending the day’s official fixing. Earlier in the week, trading at the official window saw intraday fluctuations between ₦1,349.25 and ₦1,354 per dollar, with interbank turnover reaching $248.07 million across 144 deals. In the parallel market, commonly referred to as the black market, the naira continues to trade at a significant discount to the official rate. Currency dealers across Lagos and Abuja quoted the dollar between ₦1,411 and ₦1,420 for buying, while selling rates ranged from ₦1,419 to ₦1,430 per dollar depending on transaction volume and location. This leaves an exchange rate gap of roughly ₦68 to ₦80 per dollar between the official NFEM benchmark and street-level rates. Market analysts attribute the recent softening of the local currency to heightened seasonal foreign exchange demand from importers and travelers heading into the end-of-year period, alongside foreign portfolio investment outflows and a firmer US dollar globally. Despite the recent dip—which saw the parallel market touch a 10-month low of ₦1,430 per dollar this week—Nigeria’s gross external reserves remain sturdy at approximately $54.9 billion, well above the CBN’s full-year target of $51.04 billion, offering a substantial buffer to support market liquidity through the remainder of the fourth quarter. Traders and businesses continue to monitor daily NFEM liquidity injections and CBN updates for direction as Thursday’s trading progresses. item.title: ACF crisis deepens
item.description: Moves to resolve the lingering supremacy battle within the ranks of the Arewa Consultative Forum (ACF) have yet to produce results after a closed-door meeting by members of the Board of Trustees (BoT), the National Executive Committee (NEC) and some first-class emirs from the northern region ended in what some sources described as “deadlock.” Daily Trust learnt that the meeting, which took place on Tuesday at the private residence of the Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Muhammadu Sa’ad Abubakar III, in Maitama, Abuja, lasted two hours between 5pm and 7pm without any tangible resolutions reached. The traditional rulers at the meeting included the Etsu Nupe, Alhaji Yahaya Abubakar, and the Aku Uka of Wukari, Dr. Manu Ishaku Adda Ali. The Sultan was reportedly not at the meeting as he was attending to other matters of national importance somewhere. Although the details of the meeting, which was convened at the instance of the Sultan, were sketchy, sources privy to the happenings in the ACF confided in Daily Trust that the gathering focused on resolving the worsening division in the leadership of the northern socio-political group. One of the sources said both the Etsu Nupe and the Aku Uka expressed serious reservations over the inability of the BoT and NEC to arrive at a neutral ground and work together towards finding solution to the security and economic challenges afflicting the North. “In fact, one of the emirs alluded to the fact that the North is now a laughing stock…That we cannot speak with one voice at a critical moment of our existence,” he said. Our correspondents report that the meeting on Tuesday was a continuation of series of engagements with contending parties (NEC and BoT) towards resolving the protracted leadership crisis occasioned by alleged financial impropriety. Daily Trust learnt that the Sultan, with the support of the Emir of Lafia, Justice Sidi Dauda Bage Muhammad and other northern traditional rulers have been having talks with the ACF leaders since the beginning of 2026 when the BoT and NEC engaged in blame game. On one hand, the Chairman of the BoT, Alhaji Bashir Dalhatu, with the support of some members, had asked the Secretary General of the organisation, Malam Murtala Aliyu, to leave. But Murtala had kicked saying his tenure will expire in December 2026. He reportedly has the support of some members, including the Chairman of the NEC, Barrister Mamman Mike Osuman, SAN. Besides the leadership tussle, the lodgement of about N3.9 billion donated to the ACP in a new account at JAIZ Bank, rather than in any of the main accounts of the organisation in First Bank, United Bank for Africa (UBA) and Unity Bank, has caused disaffection among members. During its 25th anniversary celebration held in November 2025, some notable northern leaders and businessmen donated the amount, in addition to pledges that are yet to be redeemed. Also, there was nearly N700 million donated by some northern leaders in order to organise the 25th anniversary
